question: What is natural law in Catholic moral teaching?

choices.A: The moral law inscribed by God in human reason and nature, accessible to all people regardless of faith through the light of reason
choices.B: The laws of physics and biology that govern the natural world
choices.C: A set of moral rules found only in the Old Testament
choices.D: The law of the strongest — the principle that what survives in nature is good

teaching.title: Natural Law
teaching.body: Natural law (lex naturalis) is the rational creature's participation in God's eternal law. Because humans are created in God's image (imago Dei) with reason, they can discern fundamental moral truths — the good to be done, evil to be avoided — without special revelation. This explains why pagan cultures independently recognize prohibitions on murder, theft, and injustice. Aquinas (Summa I-II, q.94) made natural law central to Catholic moral theology. Paul's reference to Gentiles who 'do by nature what the law requires' (Romans 2:14-15) is the key Pauline support.
